bhopal-union-carbide-gas.whole: The Bhopal plant was licensed to make 5,000 tons of methyl isocyanate-based pesticides a year. Its output peaked at 2,704 tons in 1981 and fell to 1,657 tons in 1983, about 33% of licensed capacity. Union Carbide India's losses reached Rs 50 million in the first ten months of 1984 (ICMR case study).

sources_add.title: The Bhopal Gas Tragedy (Business Ethics case study)

singrauli-ntpc.whole: By NTPC's own count, its three coal stations in the Singrauli region have 9,760 MW of installed capacity between them: Singrauli 2,000 MW, Rihand 3,000 MW and Vindhyachal 4,760 MW. NTPC says Singrauli's power goes to Uttar Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab and Delhi. No independent figures on generation were found.

chixoy-rio-negro.whole: The 300-megawatt Chixoy dam opened in 1986 and met 75% of Guatemala's electricity needs, replacing oil-burning power stations (Christian Science Monitor, 1987). It was estimated to cost $340 million and ended up at about $1 billion, two years late, after a 1983 partial collapse of its 26-mile tunnel. Guatemala then owed the Inter-American Development Bank $127 million and the World Bank $118 million for it, and about $600 million in Chixoy loans fell due within two years (Christian Science Monitor).

mumbai-urban-transport.whole: By the World Bank's own account, the Mumbai Urban Transport Project cost US$1,128 million (US$371 million IBRD loan, US$83 million IDA credit for resettlement). It added railway track and newer carriages to a suburban rail system used by more than seven million passengers a day, and the new braking system cut energy use by more than 30%. The Bank reports resettling about 100,000 people, including over 17,000 homes and almost 1,800 shops. No independent check of these figures was found.

bakolori-dam-1980-killings.whole: Bakolori was designed to irrigate 11,200 hectares by gravity and 12,000 by sprinkler and serve 40,000 to 50,000 farm families. Its construction contract grew from 174 million naira in 1974 to about 500 million naira (US$400 million) by 1982. The World Bank wrote in 1995 that "irrigation development did not occur at expected rates", and a 2000 study found farmers had poor yields from silting, erosion, flooding and crop wilting for over two decades (Nordic Journal of African Studies, 2002).

tarbela-dam.whole: By the count of WAPDA, the state authority that runs it, Tarbela has supplied 586 billion units (kWh) of hydropower to Pakistan's grid and released more than 419 million acre-feet of stored water for irrigation over 50 years. WAPDA puts the economic benefit at around $460 billion since 1974. Installed capacity is 4,888 MW, set to rise to 6,418 MW with the fifth extension (Profit/Pakistan Today, 2026). No independent check of these figures was found.

caracazo-1989.whole: The 1989 programme, backed by IMF and World Bank adjustment loans, devalued the bolívar, aimed to end budget deficits by 1991, sold state firms, freed trade and removed most subsidies and price controls. In the first half of 1991 GDP grew at about a 10% annual rate, partly from higher world oil prices; monthly inflation slowed from 3.1% in July to 1.9% in September 1991, and unemployment fell from 10.9% in 1990 to 10.3% in the first half of 1991 (GlobalSecurity.org). No poverty figures were found in the source opened.

akosombo-volta.whole: Akosombo's six turbines can generate 1,020 megawatts, though output varies with water levels; by 1967 it was also supplying Togo and Benin (Ghanaian Times). The Volta Aluminum Company (VALCO) smelter consumed half of the power generated, at highly favourable rates (UC Santa Barbara, Interdisciplinary Humanities Center). It cost £130 million in the early 1960s (Ghanaian Times).

brumadinho-dam-tuv-sud.whole: Vale's Córrego do Feijão mine produced 8.5 million tonnes of iron ore in 2018, about 2% of Vale's output that year (Kallanish). After the collapse Vale stopped about 90 million tonnes of iron ore production at affected sites, and its output fell almost 34% in the second quarter of 2019 to 64 million tonnes (Mining.com).

gambella-villagization.whole: The government presented villagization, begun in 2010 to move about 45,000 households, as a way to bring schools, clinics and clean water; the 2013 report said about 35,000 families had been gathered into 100 new or enlarged villages. A reporter's 2013 visit found a school, clinic, grinder and water in the model village of Tegni, a water pump and a school being built with community money in Pulkoat, and a broken maize grinder. Minister Shiferaw Teklemariam said "the planning, the implementation and the follow through were not as strong as you would expect" (Christian Science Monitor).

sudan-2013-fuel-subsidy.whole: The IMF backed the September 2013 fuel subsidy cut, saying subsidies mostly benefited the rich. In its own review, revenue in early 2014 was SDG 11.3 billion, over 60% higher than a year earlier, the quarter's deficit fell to 0.2% of GDP from 0.5%, and 12-month inflation fell from 41.9% at end-2013 to 35.7% at end-March 2014. Government figures then showed inflation back up to 46.8% in July 2014 (Sudan Tribune). The revenue, deficit and early inflation figures are the IMF's own; no independent check was found.

ertan-dam-resettlement.whole: Ertan has 3,300 MW of installed capacity, financed with World Bank loans of US$380 million (1991) and US$400 million (1995) plus a US$150 million loan guarantee; in 2004 its operator sold US$344 million of electricity but, selling below cost to Sichuan state firms, lost about US$15 million a year (Probe International). Resettlement cost nearly US$300 million, about three times the approved budget. The World Bank's evaluation office rated resettlement satisfactory but said it was "impossible to quantify the degree of progress" (Probe International, citing the 2005 report).

A 2013 audit by the IFC's ombudsman found the IFC had not properly vetted Dinant and that its incentives measured results in financial terms (Al Jazeera).

kainji-dam.whole: Kainji, Nigeria's first large hydroelectric plant, was built 1964-68 at an estimated US$209 million; it was designed for 960 MW but only 8 of 12 turbines were installed, giving 760 MW (Pen Global). Under the private concessionaire Mainstream Energy, which took over in 2013, a $33 million overhaul had restored 600 MW, with six of eight units working; the company said only about 30% of its invoices were being paid and the grid could not take all its power (The Guardian Nigeria).

kilwa-massacre-anvil.whole: Dikulushi was a high-grade open-pit mine producing copper-silver concentrate, 90% owned by Anvil Mining. Across its three mines Anvil produced 41,354 tonnes of copper and over a million ounces of silver in 2008; Dikulushi was put on care and maintenance in December 2008, and group staff fell from about 2,200 to 360 (IDE-JETRO company profile). No mine-level output figures were found.

itaparica-resettlement.whole: The resettlement plan, co-financed by the World Bank from 1985, promised 20,512 hectares of irrigated plots; by April 1997 only 7,787 ha (38%) were built and 2,336 of 5,917 families (39%) had plots. Spending reached about US$1.3 billion against an initial estimate of just over US$300 million. A 1997 World Bank panel found less than half the irrigation projects finished nearly ten years on, and a temporary maintenance allowance was still the main support for most families (Galvão, Cadernos de Estudos Sociais, Fundaj, 1999).

tunisia-bread-riots-1984.whole: The bread subsidy cost about 114 million dinars in 1983, about 2% of GDP, and the prime minister put the saving from the price rise at about 140 million dinars. The loaf price went from 80 to 170 millimes and flour from 120 to 295 millimes a kilo. On 6 January 1984 Bourguiba cancelled the increases and restored the subsidies (MERIP, 1984).

kedung-ombo.whole: By the Indonesian public works ministry's count, Kedung Ombo reservoir irrigates 64,365 hectares in Grobogan, Demak, Pati and Kudus, feeds 25 MW of hydropower (22.5 MW at the dam), supplies 1,700 litres a second of raw water, mostly to Semarang, and cuts peak design floods on the Serang River from 8,000 to 5,540 cubic metres a second. No independent check of these figures was found.

kyrgyz-tariffs-2010.whole: In 2010 heating rose 400% and electricity 170% after seven years of steady rates. Officials said the government needed revenue to invest in the energy sector; Prime Minister Daniyar Usenov said a kilowatt-hour cost 1.7 soms (US$0.04) to produce at the Bishkek thermal plant but sold for 0.7 som (EurasiaNet, February 2010).

mubende-kiboga-nfc.whole: By the New Forests Company's own count (reported by Oxfam in 2011), it had planted about 12 million pine and eucalyptus trees on 9,300 hectares of a roughly 20,000-hectare licence in Uganda, employed more than 1,400 people there, and built classrooms, clinics, wells and latrines. Investors included HSBC (about $10 million), the European Investment Bank (a €5 million loan) and the IFC-backed Agri-Vie fund ($6.7 million), and the company hoped to earn carbon credits. NFC said it was still developing a way to measure social impacts; no independent check was found.

arcelormittal-temirtau-mines.whole: The Temirtau steelworks, privatised to Ispat (later ArcelorMittal) in 1995, has capacity for 6 million tonnes of crude steel a year and produced about 3.4 million tonnes in most years from 2019 to 2024 (2.9 million in 2023). It employs about 35,000 people. After the October 2023 mine fire, ArcelorMittal completed the sale to the state's Qazaqstan Investment Corporation in December 2024; it was renamed Qarmet (Global Energy Monitor).

carajas-iron-ore.whole: In 1983 Carajás was expected to reach 35 million tonnes of iron ore a year by 1989, with $922 million already invested, a $305 million World Bank loan and an estimated $4.8 billion more needed (Christian Science Monitor). By 2024 Vale's Northern System, which includes Carajás, produced 177.5 million tonnes, and Vale projects 200 million tonnes a year by 2030 (InfoMoney). yacyreta.whole: Yacyretá was planned at 3,100 MW (20 turbines of 155 MW) to generate 18,940 GWh a year, mainly for Argentina. The World Bank estimated its cost at US$3.7 billion in 1979 and US$5.5 billion in 1992; by 1998 it was put at roughly US$9-10 billion, mostly from interest on delays and contractor claims. In 1998 the reservoir was held at 76 m instead of the 83 m design level, and a September 1997 World Bank document said "less than a third of the environmental and resettlement plans have been completed" (Water Power Magazine, 1998).

Bulyanhulu and North Mara together produced over 500,000 ounces of gold in 2024 (TanzaniaInvest, reporting Barrick). No independent check of these figures was found.

da-nang-quang-ngai-expressway.whole: The 139 km expressway cost VND34.5 trillion ($1.4 billion), with VND16.79 trillion from JICA and VND12.42 trillion from the World Bank. Fully opened in September 2018, it cut Da Nang to Quang Ngai travel from about three hours to a little over one. Within weeks the first section developed cracks and potholes 5-10 cm deep after heavy rain, the transport minister said asphalt quality was "not consistent", and tolls were suspended until repairs were done (VnExpress, October 2018).

casablanca-riots-1981.whole: Morocco signed a three-year, $1.1 billion IMF loan in 1980, when it had about six weeks of foreign exchange reserves. When subsidies were lifted in late May 1981, sugar rose 37%, flour 40%, butter 76% and vegetable oil 26%; after public anger the government cut the increases in half (Multinational Monitor, August 1981).

ribb-megech-irrigation.whole: The Ribb dam was reported complete in September 2017 after a five-year delay at a cost of US$160 million, with 234 million cubic metres of storage (African Leadership Magazine). A 2021 peer-reviewed study gives its irrigation area as 15,000-16,700 hectares, mostly on the Fogera plain, and reported the project "is not yet operational, as the construction of the irrigation canal system is not complete" (Mulatu et al., TU Delft).

dominican-republic-april-1984.whole: The austerity programme aimed to cut imports and government spending and boost exports to resolve a foreign-exchange and debt crisis; the IMF was withholding the second instalment of a three-year $430 million loan, and renegotiation of $2.4 billion in debt depended on an IMF deal. By September 1984 talks had resumed, exports to the US had risen, and unemployment was estimated at much more than 20% of the labour force (Christian Science Monitor). No budget or inflation results were found.

newmont-ahafo.whole: Newmont produced around 800,000 ounces of gold in Ghana in 2024. In 2025 it opened a second mine in the area, Ahafo North, at a cost of $900 million, expecting 275,000-325,000 ounces a year over 13 years and about 1,000 permanent jobs (Reuters via Mining.com). argentina-december-2001.whole: The IMF backed Argentina's peg to the dollar, raising its commitments to $22 billion in 2001. The IMF's own evaluation office found the Fund "erred in the precrisis period by supporting the country's weak policies too long" (IMF IEO, 2004).

sierra-leone-august-2022-fuel-protests.whole: The IMF programme aimed to reduce inflation and raise revenue consistent with debt sustainability. In June 2022 the IMF put end-2021 inflation at 17.9% and projected 22.1% for 2022, with growth of about 3.5%, public debt at 80.8% of non-iron-ore GDP and reserves falling from US$932 million to US$689 million; it warned that further fuel price rises could prolong fuel subsidies (IMF press release, June 2022). These are the lender's figures; no independent check was found.

ethiopia-kenya-power-line-kenya.whole: The line can carry up to 2,000 MW; Ethiopia began commercial sales to Kenya in November 2022 under a 25-year, 600 MW deal and aims to earn up to $100 million a year (The EastAfrican). In the year to June 2025 Ethiopia supplied 1,274 GWh, 83% of Kenya's electricity imports, which made up 10.6% of Kenya's energy mix, according to Kenya's energy regulator EPRA (AllAfrica).

zambia-june-1990.whole: In 1990 Zambia's foreign debt was about US$7 billion against a 1988 GDP of US$2.7 billion; inflation was running at 60%, copper earned 90% of foreign exchange, and output had fallen to an estimated 430,000 tonnes from a 1969 peak of 720,000. Per capita income had fallen 30% over 12 years. The plan aimed at 3% growth and a deficit below 2% of GDP; in May 1990 the government announced partial privatisation (South African Institute of International Affairs, 1990).

siguiri-area-one.whole: By AngloGold Ashanti's own filing with the US SEC, its Guinean subsidiary paid the government US$32.83 million in 2023, including US$30.06 million in taxes and no royalties. In 2023 a leach tank failure at the Siguiri plant cut gold output and raised costs; group output fell from 2.672 to 2.593 million ounces (Kitco). No Siguiri production figure and no independent check of the payments were found.

nigeria-anti-sap-1989.whole: Under the Structural Adjustment Programme the naira fell from N2 to the dollar in 1986 to N22.05 in 1993, and inflation rose from 5.72% to 59.97% over seven years. Total external debt rose from $14.98 billion in 1986 to $22.68 billion in 1990, and the poverty rate rose from 12% to 13.6% between 1985 and 1993, while agriculture and industry GDP rose in nominal naira (BusinessDay).

kosovo-hade-shala.whole: The Sibovc South-West mine supplies lignite to Kosovo A and B, which the World Bank Inspection Panel called "two outdated and increasingly unreliable power plants"; the Panel put Kosovo's lignite reserves as the third largest in Europe. The related World Bank project's second additional financing (US$3.9 million, 2013) paid for air, soil and water monitoring, an environmental study for a proposed power plant, monitoring of the Shala resettlement plan, an expert panel and a low-carbon growth study; Bank management said all 63 physically resettled families had been compensated (Inspection Panel report, 2015). The Panel found Bank staff failures "contributed to significant delays" in resettlement (Climate Home News).

yemen-fuel-riots-2005.whole: In July 2005 the government lifted subsidies on all oil products, saying it would support the budget and cut the deficit: oil product prices rose 100%, diesel 200% and gas 50%, after sustained pressure from the World Bank and IMF to cut subsidies and add a sales tax (Inter Press Service, 21 July 2005). No data on the fiscal result were found in sources opened.

parej-east-coal.whole: Parej East was one of 24-25 Coal India mines under two World Bank projects: a coal sector rehabilitation loan of US$530 million, cut to about US$261 million and cancelled in July 2000, and a US$63 million (later US$48 million) social and environmental mitigation credit. Bank management reported that 79% of a sample of 337 entitled people at Parej East had kept or raised their real incomes, while the requesters said "income restoration has not taken place" (Inspection Panel eligibility report). No mine output figure and no independent check of the income figure were found.

angola-diesel-protests-2025.whole: The finance minister said fuel subsidies had cost about 4% of GDP the previous year; the July 2025 rise took diesel from 300 to 400 kwanza a litre, part of a phased removal to shore up public finances as Angola faced about $9 billion of external debt payments in 2025 (Business Day/Reuters). IMF head Kristalina Georgieva put the subsidies at 2.5% of GDP and said they benefit the wealthiest; the Kwenda cash transfer programme reaches 1.7 million people (Lusa/VerAngola, November 2025).

gazela-bridge-roma-eviction.whole: The €77 million project, with a €33 million EIB loan, upgraded the Gazela bridge on Belgrade's E70/E75 motorway, which the EIB considered crucial for safety after new cracks in January 2010 forced lane and heavy-vehicle restrictions, plus 24.2 km of access roads and a 17.3 km ring road. The City of Belgrade committed to finance 80 social housing units by end-2010 for resettled families, and an audit found 80% of the temporary container units were leaking (EIB Complaints Office conclusions report).

nigeria-endbadgovernance-2024.whole: In June 2024 the World Bank approved $2.25 billion to back Nigeria's move to a market exchange rate and the phase-out of the gasoline subsidy, which it called "costly, regressive, and opaque", alongside a targeted cash transfer programme (World Bank). Petrol prices rose nearly 488% by October 2024 and the naira fell from about 465 to nearly 1,465 per dollar. In October 2025 the Bank reported higher growth and revenue and a strong external position, while projecting 139 million Nigerians in poverty by end-2025, up from 87 million in 2023 (AllAfrica).

rusumo-falls-hydro.whole: By the World Bank's completion report, the 80 MW Rusumo plant began commercial operation on 1 February 2025, with power split equally among Burundi, Rwanda and Tanzania. It generated 450 GWh by 31 August 2025 against a 448 GWh target, with about 1.25 million direct beneficiaries. Financing totalled about US$405 million, US$309 million from the World Bank, and the Bank rated the outcome "Moderately Satisfactory", with efficiency rated modest. No independent check was found.

A 2009 government report said it had been built without an environmental assessment; it was shut in 2008 and 2009, reopened each time, and closed for good in 2014 (Quartz).

rosia-montana-gabriel-resources.whole: The mine was never built. Roșia Montană Gold Corporation, formed with the Romanian state, planned to extract about 300 tonnes of gold and 1,600 tonnes of silver; Gabriel Resources said it had spent about US$500 million by 2012, and the company was the town's biggest employer where unemployment was above 70% (The Black Sea, 2013). After mass protests in 2013 the government dropped a law to fast-track the mine, and Gabriel claimed at least $3.3 billion from Romania at ICSID (Inequality.org).

The 75 km, 220 kV double-circuit line with 188 towers was Nepal Electricity Authority's first 220 kV line; when the project closed in December 2013 most towers were up but a disputed stretch in Kamalamai was unfinished (Inspection Panel investigation report). zimbabwe-fuel-protests-2019.whole: The finance minister's Transitional Stabilisation Programme put clearing arrears to the African Development Bank and World Bank first; the IMF called it "a comprehensive stabilisation and reform effort" but tied any new money to clearing those arrears. Foreign debt arrears were US$5.6 billion, inflation reached 42% in December 2018, and petrol rose 150% overnight on 12 January 2019 to US$3.31 a litre (Review of African Political Economy).

nathpa-jhakri.whole: The World Bank lent US$485 million in May 1989 for the Nathpa Jhakri hydropower project (loan agreement). A 2002 Himachal Pradesh University assessment, paid for by the Nathpa Jhakri Power Corporation that ran the project, found average annual income of resettled households rose from Rs 21,648 in 1996 to Rs 76,575 by 2002 (both at 1996 prices), against Rs 49,622 for control households. It put the share below the poverty line at 25.6% before and 16.8% after, measured against different poverty lines. No generation figures were found in the sources opened.

pangue-dam.whole: Pangue is a 450 MW hydroelectric dam on the Biobío that cost $367 million and supplies Chile's grid; ENDESA owns 97.5% and the IFC 2.5%. An independent review for the IFC by Dr Jay Hair (1997) concluded that "from an environmental and social perspective IFC added little, if any value"; the IFC rejected that, while accepting gaps on indigenous peoples, cultural property and dam policies (IFC statement, July 1997).

zambia-maize-riots-1986.whole: The IMF programme required Zambia to cut its budget deficit from more than 30% of GDP to around 10%; late in 1986 maize meal rose 120%, and the rise was rescinded after the riots. Foreign debt was $5.8 billion, debt service was 70% of exports, and living standards had fallen about 40% since 1977. In May 1987 Kaunda dropped the IMF programme, capping debt service at 5% of exports and restoring price controls (Christian Science Monitor, 1987).

A firm in Amsterdam quoted €544,000 (about US$620,000) to dispose of it; Trafigura instead paid a local Abidjan company US$17,000. Trafigura later paid about US$200 million to Côte d'Ivoire in 2007 and £30 million to UK claimants without admitting liability (Amnesty International, 2016).

Himachal Pradesh gets a 12% royalty on output, estimated at US$12 million a year, plus about 109 MW. In March 2014 the Bank expected the first unit to be commissioned by late March or early April 2014. No independent check of output was found.

The Bank suspended disbursements in April 2024 over resettlement in Ruaha, and the project closed in November 2024 at the government's request (World Bank factsheet, 2025). The company, Beo Čista Energija, said it would supply electricity equal to about 30,000 households' use and 80% of the Konjarnik plant's winter output (IFC, 2019). By 2012 Amayapampa had still not started production: owner Minera Nueva Vista had invested US$35 million by mid-2011, needed US$167 million to build, and employed 310 people, and the state mining company estimated about 1 million ounces of gold (La Razón via Minería de Bolivia).

ogoni-shell-niger-delta.whole: Ogoniland produced about 3% of Shell's Nigerian output before Shell withdrew its staff in January 1993 and stopped production there in mid-1993 (Human Rights Watch, 1999). In 2001 the IFC approved a US$30 million credit facility, with Shell sharing the risk, to lend to local oil-service firms in the Niger Delta, aiming at more jobs and business for Delta residents (IFC).
